examples.purpose: The Profile screen, the guide's In context: the card heads the screen under its Title, with a UPI ID to copy, a verified number, and two short account rows under a divider. Copying the handle and opening a row are the screen's own work, through their onPress.
examples.jsx:
<VStack>
  <Title title="Profile" subtitle="Your account and payments" />
  <ProfileCard
    name="Priya Sharma"
    monogram="PS"
    upiHandles={[
      { label: 'priya@jio', iconName: 'ic_copy', onPress: () => {} },
      { label: '98765 43210', iconName: 'ic_confirm' },
    ]}
  >
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      title="JioFinance+"
      showSupportText={false}
      navArrow={false}
      trailing={<Button label="Upgrade" onPress={() => {}} />}
    />
    <Divider />
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      title="Linked bank accounts"
      showSupportText={false}
      onPress={() => {}}
    />
  </ProfileCard>
</VStack>

props.name: name
props.description: One line ending in … (the header's ListItem title). Declared: User's display name shown in the header. Default "Name", from the component source.

props.name: monogram
props.description: Monogram initials for the avatar (used when `avatarSource` is not set). Default "MS", from the component source.

props.name: avatarSource
props.description: Avatar image source. When set, the avatar renders the image instead of the monogram.

props.name: badgeIcon
props.description: Registry icon for the small badge attached to the avatar's bottom-right corner. Pass `null` to hide the badge. Defaults to `'ic_qr_code'`. Default "ic_qr_code", from the component source.

props.name: upiHandles
props.description: Each handle is { label (required), iconName (UpiHandle's default ic_scan_qr_code), showIcon (default true), onPress }; onPress makes the pill a button that scales to 0.98 while pressed. A handle has no picture. Declared: UPI handle pills rendered under the name. Pass `[]` to render none.

props.name: header
props.description: Full override for the header row (avatar + name + handles). Takes precedence over the declarative header props. `modes` cascade into it.

props.name: children
props.description: Card body (the Figma "slot"). Rendered below the header divider. The card forces `context 10: jioPlus` onto every child so nested `ListItem`s and `Text`s stay on-dark. A child's own modes cannot unset that context.

props.name: showDivider
props.description: Toggles the divider between the header and the body. Defaults to `true`. Default true, from the component source.

props.name: width
props.description: Card width. Defaults to the Figma spec (`344`). Pass `'100%'` to fill the parent. Default 344, from the component source.

props.name: modes
props.description: Modes object for design-token resolution, cascaded to all children.

props.name: style
props.description: Style overrides for the card container.

gaps.text: Plain Text and ListItem support text in the body stay dark on the navy panel and almost disappear, as in Figma's own sample (Component Bug #354).
A body child's own modes override the card's on-dark modes (Component Bug #354).
List Item Style Boxed breaks the card: white boxes cover the header and rows, and the name disappears (Component Bug #354).
A long UPI handle never ends in …, so its pill runs past the card (Component Bug #354).
The header is 48 px tall where Figma's is 47 (Component Bug #354).
The QR badge's glyph is near-black (#0f0d0a) where Figma's is grey (#24262b), and the badge sits at the avatar's 45° point where Figma places it at (25, 24) (Component Bug #354).
The published Storybook is older than the installed package and still shows the older generated page (Component Bug #354).

Figma's Profile Card has one property, the body slot; the name, handles, badge, and photo are overrides there, and Premium is a variable mode. In code they are props (name, monogram, avatarSource, badgeIcon, upiHandles), and Premium is the Profile Card Appearance mode.
